en: Jātaka: The Sixth Book of Birth Stories,
Chapter on the Son Kharaputta.
6. The Vijjādharajātaka “You,
though being of noble appearance,
pay homage with hands joined in reverence, standing before one who is ugly in form.”
“Is he better than you, O King, or are you his equal?
Tell me both his name and your own.
“O King, they do not take up names or lineages.”
"O gods who have gone rightly and proceeded straight on,
I shall tell you my name:
I am Sakka, the lord of the thirty-three."
“O King of Devas, I ask you about this matter: why is it that upon seeing a bhikkhu endowed with virtuous conduct, one places him at the head and pays homage with palms joined?”
"What happiness does he obtain after passing away from here?
"He who, having seen a monk endowed with virtuous conduct,
stands before him with palms joined in reverence and pays homage;
"In this very life he gains praise,
and after the breaking up of the body, he goes to heaven.
"Today, indeed, good fortune has arisen for me!"
“Since we have seen Vāsava, the Lord of Beings,
and having seen both you, Sakka, and the bhikkhu,
I shall perform no small amount of meritorious deeds.”
“Truly, O King, those who are wise, learned, and contemplative of many things should indeed be served;
having seen both me and this bhikkhu.”
Perform abundant meritorious deeds.
Being free from anger, with a mind always serene,
and becoming one who offers hospitality to all guests;
“Having humbled my pride, I shall pay homage,
having heard the well-spoken words, O Lord of Devas.
The *Vijjādharajātaka*, the sixth.
